newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela retains some oil price windfall - official.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela retains some oil price windfall - official.

text.p: Venezuela did not maintain discrete accounts for its oil profits, but the country has retained a substantial windfall from the rise in petroleum prices since last year, a Venezuelan offical said Thursday.

Luis Raul Matos Azocar, finance minister of Venezuela, said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television that the country had reaped great benefits from oil revenues, and these funds would be set aside for a debt recovery fund and macro-economic stabilization fund.
"If you said where is the money from oil, it's very difficult to identify," Matos said. "We have some savings in the Fondo de Inversiones de Venezuela that we have kept there."

Matos said that, since Venezuela's congress required the government to balance any additional spending with cash in hand, the administration of President Rafael Caldera needed to spend the actual oil revenues.

This proccess left the impression that Venezuela has spent all the money, but actually the government had not accounted for the difference between the current price at about $17 per barrel and its budget calculation at $15 per barrel, Matos said.

"We have a budget that has been balanced," Matos said. "We have a surplus and in 1997, and we have not incorporated the new price of oil, which was higher than we expected, into the budget, so all those savings are there."
The minister also said that Venezuela had funds saved from the privatization of CANTV, among other revenues.
Matos declined comment on whether Venezuela would consider an exchange or buyback of its Brady bonds similar to a swap conducted by Brazil earlier this week.
Matos said he could not set a definitive date when Venezuela would sign an extension of its current International Monetary Fund loan, which will expire in July.

"The most important thing is that Venezuela fulfilled all the targets that we had agreed to with IMF.," Matos said. "We are going to make all decisions that will keep fiscal discipline and correct whatever deviations we have in the macroeconomic variables."
An I.M.F team will be visiting Venezuela next week, he said.

He said the proceeds of an upcoming Eurobond would be distinct from the government's overall debt strategy because Congress had approved the spending as part of an umbrella debt law, which sets a ceiling on total indebtedness.
Funds from the $315 million 10-year issue will be used to buy naval frigates, the minister said Tuesday.
The minister also said the government would send its plan to privatize the aluminum sector to Congress in two weeks.
The Venezuelan economic team was in New York to address a conference organized by the Latin American Information Services.
